title: Chapter 76: School on a Rainy Night
html:
“A boy visited my Haunted House today. He’s about eight or nine, barely speaks, and grows more excited the darker his surroundings become. What kind of condition could cause that?” Chen Ge asked directly. He had only two people to consult: He San and He Feng.

“Forensic medicine focuses on applied medicine, biology, and some chemistry. Psychology deals with mental processes, neuroscience, and psychiatry. They’re entirely different fields. Asking me won’t get you an answer.” He San sighed helplessly. “Boss, are you really going to ignore this? You haven’t posted in days, and your last livestream was even longer ago. If this continues, your popularity will fall. Look at your profile—people already say you’re out of ideas, and some are mocking the Haunted House.”

“They’re mocking my Haunted House?” That caught Chen Ge’s attention. He opened his profile and found plenty of negative comments.

“Boss, there’s a flood of short videos now, and most of them look the same. The moment you stop posting, viewers move on to someone else.”

“You’re right, but it isn’t as serious as you think,” Chen Ge replied. Fan Yu and his aunt still occupied his thoughts. Videos and livestreams were promotional tools; the black phone’s missions remained his true priority.

“If you say so. I only wanted to warn you.” A disappointed note entered He San’s voice. “Qin Guang is already established, and his studio has serious resources. The platform will promote him heavily, but I still believe your livestream will be better.”

“His content is an imitation of mine,” Chen Ge replied with a smile. Unlike other hosts, everything in his videos was authentic—and impossible to copy. “I’m far behind him in resources, connections, and followers, but when it comes to understanding and controlling fear, he’s still a novice.”

“You’re right! After all, you’re a professional.” He San paused before adding, “Boss, I suddenly remembered something.”

“What is it?”

“Do you still remember the senior of mine that you scared until she cried?”

“That description fits too many people. Just give me her name.”

“Gao Ru Xue. Her father is a psychologist and a tenured lecturer in criminal psychology. I’ll ask if she can help you tonight.”

“If she helps, I’ll buy you dinner and give you a free tour of the Haunted House’s newest scenario.” Grateful for the earnest young man’s help, Chen Ge readily promised a reward.

“Thanks, but no thanks! After my last visit, I had nightmares for several nights straight,” He San complained. “Once I fell asleep in class without noticing the lecturer walk up beside me. In my dream, a crazed doctor with a hammer chased me to the top of a staircase. Then a hand landed on my shoulder. I panicked and threw an elbow. When I opened my eyes, the lecturer’s glasses were already broken…”

Chen Ge tried to hold in his laughter, but he failed. “Alright then. I won’t force you to visit the Haunted House in the future.”

After chatting a little longer, Chen Ge hung up. Outside the bus window, rain clouds slowly swallowed the sun. When he returned to New Century Park, a crowd had gathered outside the Haunted House, with Xu Wan struggling to placate them.

“Xiao Wan, what’s the matter?”

“You’re finally back. They all want to enter the Haunted House, but without you, all I could do was ask them to wait.” Xu Wan had already removed her makeup, and anxious sweat covered her brow.

“Well done. Stay here and sell tickets. Leave the rest to me.” Chen Ge opened the gate, donned the Doctor Skull-cracker costume, and entered Murder by Midnight.

Around four in the afternoon, drizzle began to fall and the clouds thickened. Many outdoor rides shut down for safety, sending visitors who were not ready to leave toward indoor attractions. The Haunted House became an unlikely favorite. A large crowd remained outside until five, when it finally began to disperse.

After running through the building all afternoon, Chen Ge was exhausted. He removed his costume and stepped outside.

The sky was dark, and the wind was howling.

It was pouring like this when Fan Yu’s parents disappeared.Chen Ge regarded the sky with mixed emotions. After sending Xu Wan home, he returned to the maintenance room and packed his bag.

He packed a lighter, flashlight, multipurpose mallet, and Xiaoxiao, then left the Haunted House in a raincoat. The unexpected crowds had delayed him until six. He hailed a taxi outside the park, but the driver refused the moment he heard the destination.

Chen Ge had no choice but to wait for another. The second driver warned that shrubs had swallowed the roads near Mu Yang High School, making them impassable by car. He could only drop Chen Ge somewhere nearby.

The mission had a deadline. Arriving early would give him more time to scout the site and reduce the risk, so he quickly settled on a fare and departed.

Along the way, he asked about Mu Yang High School, but the driver kept a grave expression and stared fixedly at the road. Chen Ge found himself missing the talkative uncle who had driven him to Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy.

Around seven, they reached the end of the road. The route had been terrible, and the area felt more remote than the deepest countryside.

“The car cannot continue any further, so this is where I’ll have to stop.” The driver pointed outside the window. “There should be people living nearby, so go to them if you’re lost. Send me the fare through WeChat; I don’t accept cash.”

“No cash?” Puzzled, Chen Ge decided not to question the man’s peculiarities. He paid electronically and climbed out.

The rain intensified beneath a lightless sky. Several rows of houses stood in the distance, but every window was dark, making them appear abandoned.

“How am I supposed to find Mu Yang High School?”

Chen Ge turned to ask the driver, only to see him fling the rear seat cover through the window and speed away without hesitation.

He refused to take my cash and tossed out the mat I sat on earlier… what is the meaning of this? Is it because he thinks I’m dirty?
